newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's BCP soars near 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's BCP soars near 10 pct.

text.p: Shares in Banco Comercial Portugues (BCP) rose 9.6 percent on Friday, hitting successive record highs, as the bank appeared to be the biggest gainer from the euphoria sweeping through the Portuguese bourse.

The strong buying of Portuguese stocks was triggered by a revised rating of the bourse by Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) which announced it was promoting it to developed from emerging market status.
BCP was one of the stocks that benefited most, traders said, particularly after the New York opening.
The PSI20 bourse index was up 4.44 percent.
BCP was trading at 2,900 escudos, slightly down from its high of 2,930, compared with its previous close on Wednesday at 2,646 escudos. Thursday was a holiday in Portugal.
"BCP, along with other stocks, is benefiting from Portugal's switch to becoming a developed market," said one trader.
The shares were also being helped by the good tone in New York and by a recent analysis by UBS that said the share was worth 3,000 escudos.
